app.current_user_id is NOT set, so user-keyed policies deny — asserted directly, not inferred

migrationCompatibility.notes: No migration. The stable release connects as postgres, the table owner, which is exempt from RLS — so setting one GUC instead of none changes nothing for it. A candidate connected as juli_app gains shop-scoped rows where it previously had none.

rollbackAssertion.postCutoverFailureBehavior: reverting returns analytics_backfill_topup to system_scope, which under juli_app reads zero rows and completes silently. Nothing deployed breaks; the task resumes doing nothing.

doNotInfer: Do not claim reaper needs no exemption. It enumerates workflow_runs fleet-wide and unfiltered; Celery's active/reserved/scheduled inspection is the per-run LIVENESS PROBE, not the work list. ADR-089 decision 5 originally said otherwise and is corrected in this change — four of the five tasks need an exemption, not three.

Do not have with_shop_scope set the user GUC to keep a user-keyed query working. Withholding it is the property being bought: a shop-level beat task must not be able to read users or shops. If a query needs a user, it is not shop-scoped work.

Do not resolve a user id to satisfy with_tenant_scope instead. Reading shops.user_id requires app.current_user_id already set, so the lookup needs the context it is trying to produce; a SECURITY DEFINER owner lookup would grant an exemption to a task that needs none (ADR-089 decision 5).

Do not make _shop_scope_active a module global to match _system_scope_active. That global is a known concurrency hazard — two coroutines in one event loop share it and one can clear the other's exemption. The ContextVar is asserted by a concurrency test; copying the global makes that test fail.

Do not treat a green run of this task as evidence after the cutover. The failure mode is a successful no-op, so the integration proof must show rows written for the intended shop and none for another.
